newsitem.title: POLAND: LG Group to invest $2.5 bln in Europe by 2000.
newsitem.headline: LG Group to invest $2.5 bln in Europe by 2000.

text.p: Korea's LG Group plans to invest $2.5 billion in Europe by the year 2000, including $1.5 billion in the former Soviet Union, $700 million in Poland and $100 million in Bulgaria, LG Group officials said on Thursday.

"LG Group will invest $2.5 billion in this region (Europe) by the year 2000," deputy-president Dze Kop Sung told a news conference on the first day of LG Group's annual strategy meeting held in Warsaw.
"Investment in Poland is planned at about $700 million, in the chemical, electronic, and construction sectors," he added.
Managing director of global operations at LG Group Chong Suk Li, also present, said investment in the countries formerly making up the Soviet Union would be 1.5 billion.
Chong Suk Li also said LG Group would invest $100 million in setting up PCS personal communication technology and about $400 million in construction in Poland.
He also said the Korean firm would invest $100 million in setting up a soda production plant in Bulgaria until the end of the century.
